title: Introduce secret-mesh Terraform module for KMS/HSM <-> Vault/SecretsManager synchronization
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a composable Terraform module called 'secret-mesh' that provisions a secrets synchronization layer for Private (VPC) deployments. The module will provide a configurable control-plane shim and optional operator for reconciling secrets between cloud KMS/HSM providers and runtime secret stores (HashiCorp Vault and cloud Secrets Manager). Goals: 1) reliable, auditable one-way or bidirectional secret sync for onboarding private deployments; 2) automated health checks and drift detection with self-heal or alert-only modes; 3) explicit upgrade path for key rotations and module upgrades with minimal downtime; 4) pluggable adapters for Cloud KMS, PKCS#11 HSM proxies, and Vault transit envelope encryption. The module should be usable by both the Private product and Dedicated-reserved environments where customers manage a KMS/HSM in their VPC. Include integration tests, docs, and migration guide for existing terraform users.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes variables to configure primary KMS provider, optional HSM adapter endpoint, Vault cluster address, and cloud Secrets Manager target
Module creates IAM/service accounts, KMS key bindings, and Vault role/policy scaffolding without storing secrets in state
Healthcheck outputs: last-successful-sync timestamp, per-target drift count, and an alerting webhook URL output
Supports two sync modes: 'push-to-vault' (cloud KMS -> Vault) and 'mirror' (bidirectional) with explicit conflict resolution policy
Module includes a canary upgrade path that stages new key wrapping policies and allows atomic rollout of adapter changes
E2E test runs in CI that provisions a small VPC sandbox, bootstraps mock KMS/HSM (emulated PKCS#11) and Vault, exercises key rotation and verifies no secret leakage
Documentation added: Terraform usage, upgrade guide, security considerations, and troubleshooting section
At least one customer-facing Private deployment uses the module in pilot and reports no secret-access regressions
design_decisions: Provide a thin control-plane Terraform module that can optionally deploy a Kubernetes operator; prefer operator for long-lived clusters where reconciliation latency matters
Default to server-side envelope encryption using Vault Transit when available; fall back to cloud KMS-wrapped values if Vault not present
Avoid storing plaintext secrets or KMS private material in Terraform state by managing only roles, bindings, and operator configs; secrets live in Vault/Secrets Manager
Implement drift detection as a read-only reconciliation step that can be run on schedule and emits prometheus metrics and alerts
Expose adapter interface so future HSM vendors can be added without rewriting module (adapter = config blob + healthcheck probe endpoint)
tradeoffs: Operator vs pure Terraform: operator gives better runtime reconciliation but increases operator support surface and runtime dependencies
Transactional sync complexity: fully transactional multi-target sync is expensive; chosen approach is best-effort with idempotent reconciliation and conflict-resolution policies to avoid deadlocks
Supporting PKCS#11 HSM proxies requires additional infra in customer VPCs; prioritizing a minimal adapter shim to reduce ops burden
Keeping secrets out of state reduces convenience for some workflows (manual bootstrap) but is non-negotiable for security compliance
implementation_plan: Week 1: Design review and finalize module API (variables, outputs), define adapter interface and healthcheck contract
Week 2: Implement Terraform resources for IAM, KMS keys, and Vault bootstrap (roles/policies); add outputs for monitoring and webhook endpoints
Week 3: Build optional Kubernetes operator scaffolding (helm chart) and a lightweight adapter container that implements PKCS#11 proxy or cloud KMS client
Week 4: Add healthcheck lambda/controller that reports sync metrics and drift counts; wire prometheus exporter and Grafana dashboard snippets
Week 5: E2E CI tests and integration with staging Private environment; documentation and migration guide
Week 6: Pilot with one customer/private deployment, collect feedback and iterate
test_plan: Unit tests for module input validation and template rendering
Integration tests in CI using terraform-integration harness: provision temporary VPC, bootstrap Vault dev server, run sync in push and mirror modes
Chaos test: simulate network partition to adapter and verify reconciliation catches drift and self-heals when connectivity returns
Security test: verify no secret values are written to terraform state and that access logs are generated for key-usage audit
